title: Downtown Fergus rezoning approved after reconsideration
subtitle: Elora balcony encroachment, fire pumper truck award, open-air burning changes, EV chargers, and water supply update.
overview: Council first defeated the rezoning for a five-storey, 17-unit rental building at 223 St. Andrew St. E. in Fergus {{vote:m7}}, because an abstention counts as a negative vote. After a recess, Council voted to reconsider {{vote:m8}} and then approved the rezoning {{vote:m9}}. The related zoning by-law was passed {{vote:m12}}. The approval allows a height of 16.7 metres. Parking, design and site plan details still go through later review.

In Elora, Council approved a heritage permit {{vote:m5}} and an encroachment agreement {{vote:m6}} so a balcony can be rebuilt over the sidewalk at the former Commercial Hotel building, with conditions on clearances, lighting, insurance and inspections.

Council also approved changes to the open-air burning by-law {{vote:m2}}, awarded the fire pumper truck contract {{vote:m3}}, adopted the 2024 Community Improvement Plan programs {{vote:m4}}, and committed $21,500 toward a grant for eight public EV chargers {{vote:m10}}. A water supply update was received for information {{vote:m11}}. Presentations covered the Fergus Scottish Festival and local physician recruitment.

decisions.detail: After reconsideration, Council approved the zoning amendment allowing a 16.7 m, five-storey mixed-use building with 17 rental units in downtown Fergus.
Council authorized an encroachment agreement for a cantilevered balcony over the sidewalk at 43 West Mill Street, with clearance, lighting, insurance and inspection conditions.

decisions.item: Heritage permit for West Mill Street
decisions.detail: Council approved the heritage permit for alterations at 27-43 West Mill Street, Elora, with the conditions in the staff report.
Council awarded the pumper truck contract to Dependable Emergency Vehicles at an upset limit of $1,093,377 excluding HST.
Council approved changes to the burning by-law, including a new one-time Class D permit and clearer rules on where fires are permitted, and directed staff to draft the amendment.
Council activated six incentive programs for 2024 and delegated approvals and signing authority to staff.
Council committed $21,500 toward a grant application for eight public EV chargers, four each in Fergus and Elora.

debate: On the Fergus rezoning, supporters pointed to the need for rental and accessible housing, intensification to protect farmland, and the redesign with a stepped-back fifth storey and the building moved away from its neighbour.

Opponents of the rezoning raised parking: a downtown that is already near capacity, 13 on-site spaces for 17 units plus commercial space, and the stacking of several projects at once before a parking strategy is in place. Staff said extra spaces nearby could be secured at site plan and the parking strategy did not criticize the 50% reduction.

On the Elora balcony, one councillor worried about precedent for building over Township property. Staff said the design changed to a cantilever with removable, non-structural columns, the property is designated heritage, and similar requests would normally be refused.

Councillors asked about winter snow clearing and accessibility around the balcony columns. Staff said the clear path exceeds the Township's minimum sidewalk width and the columns could be removed if snow removal became a problem.

On water supply, one councillor asked about the nearly fourfold capacity increase planned for the Well F2 replacement. Staff said a public Class EA study will consult nearby residents and assess impacts.
